questions.text: How does the source define restrictive lung disease?

answers.text: Diseases that restrict lung expansion, causing decreased lung volume and increased work of breathing
Diseases with airflow limitation that is not fully reversible
Repeated episodes of no airflow during sleep
Sudden blockage of a pulmonary artery

questions.text: In the source mnemonic PAINT, what does P represent?

answers.text: Pleural disorders
Pulmonary hypertension
Pneumonia only
Peak flow

questions.text: What is the primary PFT test to diagnose restrictive disease in the source?

answers.text: Lung volumes
Sweat chloride
D-dimer ELISA
Polysomnography
Any abnormal, excessive amount of fluid in the pleural space
Air entering the pleural space after an airway rupture
Blood in the pulmonary artery
Inflammation of the alveoli from infection only

questions.text: Which pairing correctly matches pleural effusion type and protein pattern?

answers.text: Transudative effusion has decreased proteins; exudative effusion has increased proteins
Transudative effusion has increased proteins; exudative effusion has decreased proteins
Both transudative and exudative effusions have no proteins
Protein pattern is used only for sleep apnea

questions.text: Which finding is listed for pleural effusion diagnosis?

answers.text: Tracheal deviation away from the affected lung
Tracheal deviation toward the affected lung in every case
A positive sweat chloride test
A crescendo-decrescendo breathing pattern

questions.text: Which patient pattern matches primary spontaneous pneumothorax in the source?

answers.text: Late teens to early twenties, tall, thin, male, without underlying lung disease
Hospitalized for 2 days within the last 90 days
Positive PPD with no symptoms
COPD with coexisting OSA

questions.text: Why can tension pneumothorax rapidly become fatal?

answers.text: Mediastinal shift can prevent venous return, eliminating cardiac output
It always causes increased sweat chloride
It blocks apoptosis in lung cells
It only causes mild daytime sleepiness

questions.text: Bronchopleural fistula is described as a pneumothorax involving:

answers.text: A large airway such as mainstem, lobar, or segmental airway
Only the pharyngeal airway during sleep
Only the pulmonary artery
Only a lymph node granuloma

questions.text: Interstitial lung disease is characterized by:

answers.text: Fibrosis and/or inflammation affecting the lung parenchyma
Only upper airway closure during sleep
Only a clot from a lower extremity vein
Only productive cough for 3 months per year

questions.text: Sarcoidosis is described in the source as:

answers.text: An idiopathic multisystem disorder with inflammatory cells collecting in granulomas
A venous clot blocking a pulmonary artery
An acute lower respiratory tract infection only
A traumatic blood collection in the pleural space

questions.text: Which diagnostic pattern is listed for interstitial lung disease?

answers.text: Restrictive pattern on FVC and plethysmography with decreased DLCO
Increased FEV1/FVC with positive IGRA only
AHI greater than 30 events/hr only
Sweat chloride less than 40 mEq/L

questions.text: Myasthenia gravis is caused by antibodies that block or destroy:

answers.text: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the nerve-muscle junction
Pulmonary artery catheter balloons
Endotracheal tube biofilms
Upper airway dilator muscles only during sleep

questions.text: Guillain-Barre syndrome involves immune attack on:

answers.text: The myelin sheath of peripheral nerves
The pleural space by hydrostatic pressure
The CFTR protein in sweat glands
Cancer cells through apoptosis

questions.text: During a sniff test for phrenic nerve damage, paradoxical movement means:

answers.text: The affected side moves upward during vigorous inspiration
The patient has an AHI less than 5
The P/F ratio rises above 400
The sputum culture becomes positive
